function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization that gives a financial institution (or another service provider) permission to act on your behalf. Think of it as a written agreement where you grant someone the authority to perform certain actions—such as making payments, managing investments, or handling other financial tasks—for you. Key points: | Aspect | Explanation | |--------|-------------| | **Purpose** | Allows a third party (e.g., bank, investment firm) to execute transactions or manage assets without needing your constant approval. | | **Common Types** | • **Direct Debit / Standing Order** – recurring payments.
• **Investment Mandate** – instructions on how to invest funds.
• **Payment Mandate** – authorizing a specific payment. | | **Status Categories** | • **Active** – currently in effect.
• **Pending** – awaiting confirmation or activation.
• **Inactive** – expired, cancelled, or not yet activated. | | **Benefits** | • Convenience: automated transactions.
• Security: clear legal framework protects both parties.
• Transparency: records show who authorized what. | In short, a mandate is a legally binding document that tells a financial institution exactly what it can do on your behalf, and its status indicates whether it's currently valid, waiting to start, or no longer in force.
